title: Reword a question that fails the design
statement: When a judged question fails most items because of a deliberate design choice, reword it before it gates anything.
example: One screenshot question failed 24 of 30 pages, all on a layout chosen on purpose.
detail: A screenshot judge's question asking whether the task was the most prominent thing on screen failed 24 of 30 pages of one lesson, every one on a split layout that keeps the passage beside its question on purpose (`grade3-reading/artifacts/cert-layer/VISION-QA-CALIBRATION-2026-08-31.md`). The calibration concluded that a question failing 80% of a lesson's screens on a documented, intentional layout has low information value as worded, and would need rewording, for example to ask whether the split is reasonable, before it could inform a gate (the same file).
against: The same run asked for a person to look at whether any of the 24 pages had a real layout problem despite the deliberate design (`grade3-reading/artifacts/cert-layer/VISION-QA-CALIBRATION-2026-08-31.md`).

evidence.quote: layout choice has low information value as currently worded
